সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: 34) ১৯৭২ সালের সংবিধানে মোট কতটি তফসিল ছিলো?

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: 36) ‘‘The Comedy of Manners” is commonly associated with -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- Comedy of manners is a genre of comedy that involves sophisticated wit and talent.
- Its distinguishing feature is a less physical action and more heavy dialogue.
- Most of the best plays of comedy of manners were written during the Restoration Age.
- The restoration age of English literature is roughly from 1660 to 1700.
- The restoration refers to the restoration of the monarchy after the puritan rebellion.
- Comedy of manners satirises the manners and ways of middle and upper-middle-class people who were also their audience.
- William Congreve and Willaim Wycherley were major contributors to the comedy of manners during the Restoration age.
- Therefore, from all the given points we can infer that the comedy of manners is commonly associated with the Restoration Age.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৩৭) 'Mosca' is an important character in -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:

• It's important characters:
- Volpone,
- Mosca,
- Celia,
- Voltore,
- Corbaccio,
- Castrone
- Bonario,
- Corvino etc.
Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica and Volpone by Ben Jonson.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৩৮) Who called Shakespeare an ‘upstart crow’ in his book titled A Groats-Worth of Wit?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Robert Greene was an Elizabethan dramatist and pamphleteer.
He wrote a pamphlet called A Groats-Worth of Wit bought with a million Repentance in 1592.
It is believed that he called Shakespeare an upstart crow.
Upstart means someone who claimed the socio-political ladder but does not have the required skills and crow is known for stealing from others.
Thus, Robert Greene believed that Shakespeare doesn't deserve the success he got because he do not have formal training and steals from other writers.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question:
৩৯) 'Far from the madding crowd’s ignoble strife
Their sober wishes never learn’d to stray' – this line was quoted by
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
লাইনটি Thomas Gray-এর লেখা Elegy written in the Country Churchyard নামক কবিতা থেকে নেওয়া হয়েছে।
Far from the madding crowd নামে Thomas Hardy-এর একটি উপন্যাস আছে। তাই, Far from the madding crowd -কথাটুকু দেখে মনে হতে পারে যে এটা Thomas Hardy-এর লেখা উপন্যাসের লাইন।
কিন্তু মনে রাখতে হবে যে, Far from the madding crowd কথাটুকু Hardy-এর লেখা উপন্যাসের নাম হলেও, এই পুরো লাইনটি আসলে Thomas Gray-এর কবিতার ভিতরের বিখ্যাত লাইন।

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪০) "Mephistopheles" in Doctor Faustus is a/an -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Doctor Faustus, in full The Tragicall History of D. Faustus, tragedy in five acts by Christopher Marlowe, published in 1604 but first performed a decade or so earlier.
Marlowe’s play followed by only a few years the first translation into English of the medieval legend on which the play is based.

In Doctor Faustus Marlowe retells the story of Faust, the doctor-turned-necromancer, who makes a pact with the devil in order to obtain knowledge and power.
Both Doctor Faustus and Mephistopheles, who is the devil’s intermediary in the play, are subtly and powerfully portrayed.

Marlowe examines Faustus’s grandiose intellectual ambitions, revealing them as futile, self-destructive, and absurd.

Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪১) Which theatre in London did Shakespeare associate with?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Shakespeare was associated with the Globe Theatre.
It is a very famous historical theatre in London.
The Globe, which opened in 1599, became the playhouse where audiences first saw some of Shakespeare's best-known plays. 

Source: www.folger.edu

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪২) The hero of 'The Rape of the Lock' is -

• His famous epic is The Rape of the Lock.

- Baron (Hero),
- Belinda (Heroine),
- Arial (God).
Source: The Rape of the Lock.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪৩) 'The Pilgrim's Progress' is a famous allegory in prose written by -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
The Pilgrim’s Progress, a religious allegory by the English writer John Bunyan, published in two parts in 1678 and 1684.
The work is a symbolic vision of the good man’s pilgrimage through life. At one time second only to the Bible in popularity, The Pilgrim’s Progress is the most famous Christian allegory still in print.
Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪৪) Who is a Cavalier poet?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Cavalier poet, any of a group of English gentlemen poets, called Cavaliers because of their loyalty to Charles I (1625–49) during the English Civil Wars, as opposed to Roundheads, who supported Parliament.
They were also cavaliers in their style of life and counted the writing of polished and elegant lyrics as only one of their many accomplishments as soldiers, courtiers, gallants, and wits.
The term embraces Richard Lovelace, Thomas Carew, Sir John Suckling, Edmund Waller, and Robert Herrick.

Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪৫) Choose the option which is different from the rest.
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
The writer of all the books except ‘The Jew of Malta’ is William Shakespeare, while the writer of ‘The Jew of Malta’ is Christopher Marlowe.
Hence, ‘The Jew of Malta’ is the odd one out.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৪৬) What is Spenser’s eighty-eight Petrarchan Sonnet series called?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- Edmund Spenser was an English poet who produced some of the most renowned works of poetry found in the English language during the Elizabethan period.
- His Amoretti Sonnets contains eighty-eight sonnets commemorating his courtship with Elizabeth Boyle, his second wife. 
- The word 'Amoretti' means 'little love poems.'
- It is in Petrarchan form.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫১) The Shepheardes Calender is a series of ______ eclogues, one for each month of the year.
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- Shepheardes Calender was written by Edmund Spenser and published in 1579.
- It was inspired by the eclogues of Virgil and dedicated to Sir Philip Sydney.
- Eclogues are short pastoral dramatic poems.
- Spenser wrote twelve eclogues admiring Queen Elizabeth and are named after each month of the year.
- 12 eclogues symbolise the turning of seasons in a shepherd's life.
- Therefore, The Shepheardes Calender is a series of 12 eclogues, one for each month of the year.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫২) Utopia is a ___ by Thomas More.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৩) Who was known as the ''Father of Modern English Criticism''?

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৪) Gulliver’s Travels is a novel written by Jonathan Swift combines -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- Gulliver’s Travels, original title Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World, four-part satirical work by Anglo-Irish author Jonathan Swift, published anonymously in 1726 as Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World.
- A keystone of English literature, it was one of the books that gave birth to the novel form, though it did not yet have the rules of the genre as an organizing tool.
- A parody of the then-popular travel narrative, Gulliver’s Travels combines adventure with savage satire, mocking English customs and the politics of the day.
Source: Britannica

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৫) Who is the writer of the novel 'Arcadia'?

His famous books are Arcadia (A book that bears the embryo of English Novel), The Lady of May, An Apology for Poetry.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৬) Christopher Marlow is noted especially for his -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.option2: cultivation of mystery and the macabre.
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Cristopher Marlowe was the greatest dramatist before Shakespeare.
- Christopher Marlowe, (baptized Feb. 26, 1564, Canterbury, Kent, Eng.—died May 30, 1593, Deptford, near London), Elizabethan poet and Shakespeare’s most important predecessor in English drama, who is noted especially for his establishment of dramatic blank verse. 

Some of Marlowe's literary works:
- Doctor Faustus,
- The Jew of Malta,
- Tamburlaine the Great

Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৭) Who is known as a “Metaphysical Poet”?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Metaphysical poet, any of the poets in 17th-century England who inclined to the personal and intellectual complexity and concentration that is displayed in the poetry of John Donne, the chief of the Metaphysicals.
Other Metaphysical poets are:
- Henry Vaughan,
- Andrew Marvell,
- John Cleveland,
- Abraham Cowley
- George Herbert and
- Richard Crashaw.

Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৮) The poem 'Piers Plowman' was written by -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Piers Plowman (in full The Vision of Piers Plowman), a satirical poem, was written by William Langland.
Three versions of Piers Plowman are extant:
- A, the poem’s short early form, dating from the 1360s;
- B, a major revision and extension of A made in the late 1370s; and
- C, a less “literary” version of B dating from the 1380s and apparently intended to focus the work’s doctrinal issues.
The poem takes the form of a series of dream visions dealing with the social and spiritual predicament of late 14th-century England.

Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৫৯) Who wrote the novel “Robinson Crusoe”?

Robinson Crusoe is a novel by Daniel Defoe, first published on 25 April 1719. The first edition credited the work's protagonist.
- Daniel Defoe (1660 - 1731) is an English novelist, pamphleteer, and journalist.
- Daniel Defoe also wrote:
- Moll Flanders (1722)
- A Journal Of the Plague Year
- Captain Singleton

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬০) Which of the following writers does not belong to the Augustan Age?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
In the Augustan Age (1702-1745), there were some prominent writers such as:

- Joseph Addison
- Jonathan Swift
- Daniel Defoe
On the other hand,
- Oliver Goldsmith is a writer of the Age of Johnson (1745-1785).

Source: An ABC of English Literature.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬১) Euphues was written by John Lyly in 1579. What was the subtitle of Euphues?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- John Lyly was one of the University Wits, a group of dramatists who all graduated from Oxford or Cambridge.
- He gained prominence due to his prose romances Eupheus: The Anatomy of Wits and Euphues and His England.
- His literary style inspired Euphuism, a writing form that uses excessively ornate language and literary devices to display the knowledge of a writer.
- Subtitles in literature usually add details about the work or even act as an alternative title.
- Lyly's work Euphues's plot is not that necessary as it's just a structure to hold the dialogues and conversations.
- Therefore, from all the points given above, we can infer that the subtitle of Eupheus is The Anatomy of Wit.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৩) 'Novum Organuma' is a philosophical work in Latin by -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- Novum organum is a philosophical work in Latin (1620) by Francis Bacon, presenting an inductive method for scientific and philosophical inquiry.
- Sir Francis Bacon's ''Novum Organum'' is a treatise meant to adjust the thought and methodology of learning about and understanding science and nature. - The origination point of the Novum Organum was in Bacon's perception that the scientific process or method of his time was woefully inadequate to get to the bottom of deep and important questions about nature and knowledge.
- The system Bacon eventually proposed was what we know as the scientific method, a process by which one, through inductive principles and empirical data gathered through observation, can find precise answers to natural and scientific phenomena.
- Up until this time, Sir Francis saw the educational methods of his peers as completely disjointed and separated from reality.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৪) Which one of the following authors does not belong to the Elizabethan Age?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- John Milton is the author who does not belong to the Elizabethan Age.
- The Elizabethan Age is the age during the age of Elizabeth which lasted from 1558 - 1603.
- John Milton lived from 1608 to 1674, during the Puritan Age.
- Hence we find that the correct answer is John Milton.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৫) Which one was considered the finest Elizabethan sonnet cycle?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
Sir Philip Sidney (1554 - 1586) was one of the most prominent poets of the Elizabethan era.
- His Astrophel and Stella considered the finest Elizabethan sonnet cycle.
- Sidney helped to popularize Italian poetic forms such as the sonnet and the villanelle, making them some of the most popular and enduring forms in English poetry.
- The Defence of Poesie & An Apology for Poetry also written by Sir Philip Sidney.
- The Faerie Queene was work of Edmund Spenser. 

Source: Britannica.com

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৬) Who said, “Fools rush in where angels fear to tread”?
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
"Fools rush in where angels fear to tread." This line is from “An Essay on Criticism,” by Alexander Pope.
The phrase alludes to inexperienced or rash people attempting things that more experienced people avoid.
Bangla meaning of this phrase: হাতি ঘোড়া গেলো তল, পিঁপড়া বলে কত জল / বিজ্ঞ যেথা ভয় পায়, অজ্ঞ সেথা আগে ধায়।

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৭) Who is the author of “A True Hymn” ?

- The Temple

- Affliction

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৮) ''The Conquest of Granada of the Spaniards" is a ____ written by John Dryden.

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৬৯) Who is not a university wit?

সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.question: ৭০) Paradise Lost is written in -
সমন্বিত বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (৭৫ দিনে পুরো স.exp:
- Paradise Lost is an epic poem in blank verse by the 17th-century English poet John Milton.
- An epic poem is a lengthy, narrative work of poetry.
- These long poems typically detail extraordinary feats and adventures of characters from a distant past.
- Blank verse is a literary device defined as un-rhyming verse written in iambic pentameter.
- It has a consistent meter with 10 syllables in each line (pentameter); where, unstressed syllables are followed by stressed ones, five of which are stressed but do not rhyme.
